items.stem: What most clearly distinguishes a digital twin from an ordinary 3D CAD model of an asset?

options.text: A digital twin is continuously updated with live data so it reflects the asset's current state
options.rationale: Correct: the defining feature is the live data link keeping the twin synchronised with reality.

options.text: A digital twin is simply a higher-resolution 3D render
options.rationale: Resolution is not the distinction; the live data connection is.

options.text: A digital twin must be printed in 3D
options.rationale: Printing is unrelated to what makes a twin.

options.text: A digital twin never changes once built
options.rationale: A static model never changes; a twin updates with live data.

items.explanation: Correct: the defining feature is the live data link keeping the twin synchronised with reality.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid uses of a digital twin? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Running what-if simulations to test changes before applying them physically
options.rationale: Correct: simulating scenarios on the twin avoids risky physical trials.

options.text: Predicting maintenance needs from the asset's live behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: predictive maintenance is a core twin use case.

options.text: Permanently replacing the physical asset so it can be switched off
options.rationale: A twin mirrors the asset; it does not replace the physical thing.

options.text: Guaranteeing outcomes regardless of input data quality
options.rationale: Twin insights are only as good as their data; quality matters.

items.explanation: Correct: simulating scenarios on the twin avoids risky physical trials.

items.stem: A factory twin gives misleading predictions. Investigation shows sensor data arrives hours late. What does this illustrate?

options.text: Synchronisation and data quality are essential; a twin with stale data misrepresents reality
options.rationale: Correct: a twin depends on timely, accurate data to stay a faithful mirror.

options.text: Digital twins do not need any data
options.rationale: Twins fundamentally depend on data; this is the opposite lesson.
The issue is data latency, not appearance.

options.text: Simulations are always correct regardless of inputs
options.rationale: Garbage-in produces misleading output; inputs matter.

items.explanation: Correct: a twin depends on timely, accurate data to stay a faithful mirror.
